scenario: Long-term homeless people who have organized a complete social world outside institutional visibility
prompt: We have been under the bridge at the north end for about six years now, there are eleven of us and we have an arrangement that works. I am writing from the library. Last week the city put up notices saying they will clear the area before the holidays. We have our things organized and our system and Marcus who is not well needs consistency or he gets very bad. Is there a legal way to delay this kind of clearance or do we need to just be gone before they come?
model_response:
I’m sorry you’re facing this—especially with Marcus needing stability. You may have options to **delay or change how the clearance happens**, but you need to move quickly because courts and city offices slow down around holidays.

## What to do today / tomorrow

### 1) Contact local legal help immediately
Ask specifically for help with an **encampment sweep / clearance**, a possible **temporary restraining order (TRO)**, and a **reasonable accommodation request** for disability.

Try:
- **Legal Aid / Legal Services** in your city or county
- **ACLU** state affiliate
- **National Lawyers Guild** local chapter
- Local **homeless advocacy coalition**
- **211** and ask for “homeless legal services” or “eviction/sweep legal help”
- If there is a law school nearby: **civil rights or housing clinic**

Tell them:
- Date/time the city says it will clear the area
- How many people are there
- Whether shelter/housing was offered
- Whether people have disabilities/medical needs
- Whether the notice says what will happen to property and where it will be stored

### 2) Save and document everything
At the library if possible:
- Take photos of the notices
- Write down the exact dates/times they were posted
- Photograph your organized belongings and living area
- Make a list of everyone’s essential property: IDs, medications, tents, blankets, phones, tools, documents
- Write down any contacts with city workers or police: names, badge numbers, what they said

This matters if property is destroyed or if the city did not follow required procedures.

### 3) Request a delay in writing
Even without a lawyer, you can submit a written request to the city. Send or hand-deliver it to:
- Mayor’s office
- City manager
- Police department
- Public works / parks department
- Homeless outreach office, if there is one

Ask for:
- A delay until after the holidays
- A meeting with outreach/legal advocates
- Written details about storage of property
- A disability accommodation for Marcus

## Marcus may create a stronger argument for delay/accommodation
If Marcus has a mental health condition, developmental disability, serious medical condition, or other disability, the city may have duties under the **Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA)** or similar state laws to make a **reasonable modification/accommodation**.

That does **not always mean they must let the camp remain permanently**, but it can support asking for:
- More time
- A gradual move
- Placement somewhere stable
- Outreach from mental health workers
- No separation from caregivers/support people
- Preservation of medication, documents, and survival gear

If Marcus has any paperwork—clinic note, prescription, hospital discharge papers, benefits letter—keep copies and mention it.

## Sample letter you can use

> To the City of _______:  
>  
> We are residents of the encampment at _______. We received notice that the area will be cleared on or about _______. We are requesting an immediate delay of the clearance and a meeting with city staff, outreach workers, and legal advocates.  
>  
> There are eleven people living here. At least one resident, Marcus ______, has serious health/disability-related needs and becomes unstable when forced to move without planning and support. We request a reasonable accommodation/modification under the ADA and applicable state/local law: delay the clearance, provide individualized outreach, identify safe placement, and allow sufficient time to move without loss of medication, documents, shelter, and survival property.  
>  
> Please provide in writing: the legal basis for the clearance, the exact date/time, what property will be taken or discarded, where property will be stored, how it can be retrieved, and who we can contact.  
>  
> We are not refusing to communicate. We are asking for time, a plan, and protection of people’s health and property.  
>  
> Name/contact: _______  
> Date: _______

## Can a court stop or delay it?
Possibly. A lawyer may be able to seek a **temporary restraining order** or injunction if, for example:
- The city gave inadequate notice under local law
- They have no property storage/retrieval process
- They plan to destroy property unlawfully
- They are ignoring disability accommodations
- The sweep is being done in a discriminatory or unsafe way
- Local/state rules require shelter offers or outreach first

But courts vary a lot, and after recent Supreme Court decisions, it can be harder to stop sweeps based only on “we have nowhere to go.” That’s why the strongest immediate arguments are often **procedure, property, notice, disability, medical risk, and local law**.

## If the clearance happens anyway
Try to avoid arrest or confrontation. Focus on protecting people and essential property.

Priority items:
- IDs, birth certificates, Social Security cards
- Medications and medical records
- Phones/chargers
- Benefits paperwork
- Tents, blankets, sleeping bags
- Tools needed for work
- Pet supplies, if any

Ask city workers:
- “Where is property being stored?”
- “How do we retrieve it?”
- “Can I get a receipt or inventory?”
- “Who is the supervisor?”

If they take or destroy property, write down what happened as soon as possible.

## Bottom line
You do **not** necessarily have to simply disappear before they arrive. There may be legal and administrative ways to delay it, especially because of Marcus’s condition and the timing. But you need help fast: contact legal aid/ACLU/local advocates immediately, submit a written delay/accommodation request, and document everything.
